title: Harden reranker service: adaptive timeouts, circuit breakers, multi-region fallbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: The reranking endpoint is critical for relevance-sensitive flows (search, recommendations, Q&A). We observe intermittent higher tail latencies under load and regional failures that surface as customer-facing errors. Scope: implement adaptive request timeouts, a tiered circuit breaker system per downstream reranker/embedding model, and a regional fallback/rerouting policy with graceful degradation. Goals: reduce 99th percentile latency by 30% under typical load profiles, cut customer-visible error rate originating from reranker timeouts by 5x, and provide deterministic fallback behavior during regional outages.
background_and_current_state: Current reranker call path: frontdoor -> rerank-service -> model-pool (hosted/dedicated). Problems: single static timeout (4s) that is too long for bursty tail, no circuit breakers on model-pools so cascading retries create capacity storms, and naive global failover that retries same region until timeout. Existing observability (console per-route latency) lacks a clear histogram for per-call circuit-breaker events. Related tickets ENG-4927 and ENG-7120 addressed rerank routing but did not implement adaptive failure handling.
proposed_design: 1) Adaptive timeouts: compute client-side timeout per request as max(base_timeout * load_factor, min_timeout) using recent P50/P95 latencies from the model pool. 2) Circuit breakers: implement a three-tier CB: short CB (fast-fail for transient spikes), sustained CB (trips for sustained error rate), and capacity CB (trips on high queueing latency). CB state stored in Redis with sharded keys per model-variant+region. 3) Regional routing and fallbacks: prefer local region, then precomputed regional priority list; on CB trip or region unhealthy mark, reroute to next region and return a response header with fallback reason. 4) Graceful degradation: if reranker unavailable, fall back to cheap embedding-distance rerank using cached embeddings and mark response as degraded. 5) Operational toggles: feature flag per customer for fallback policies and a kill-switch for immediate CB disabling.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route 99th percentile latency reduced by >=30% in synthetic burst tests compared to baseline
End-to-end customer-visible rerank errors due to timeouts reduced by >=5x in chaos test
Circuit-breaker events are emitted to telemetry with region/model tags and appear in Console dashboard
Fallback reroutes preserve ordering semantics and include response header X-Rerank-Fallback explaining reason
Rollout can be toggled per-customer and reverted within 5 minutes
implementation_plan: Add adaptive timeout module to rerank client (library change) and wire read of recent model-pool latency metrics via metrics cache API
Implement circuit-breaker library with Redis-backed state + in-memory failfast cache; add metrics and tags
Extend router to consult CB and region health; implement regional priority list service and local caching
Add embedding-distance fallback path using prefix KV cache for recent embeddings and ensure tie-breaking matches existing ranking heuristics
Add feature flags and admin console controls for toggles and kill-switch
Instrument telemetry (CB trips, fallback triggers, latency breakdown) and add Console dashboard panels + alerts
Run canary rollout to 10% of traffic for non-critical customers, run chaos tests, then ramp to 100%
testing_plan: Unit tests: CB state transitions, timeout calculation, fallback selection logic
Integration tests: end-to-end rerank with simulated model-pool delays and errors
Load tests: bursty traffic, verify tail latency improvement and CB efficacy
Chaos tests: region failover via network partition, verify reroute and degraded responses
Customer staging: invite two heavy rerank customers to opt into canary and gather feedback
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: rerank.cb_trips{region,model,reason}, rerank.fallbacks.total, rerank.timeouts.total, rerank.latency.p{50,95,99}
Alerts: CB triprate > threshold sustained for 5m, fallback rate > 0.5% for paid customers, regional error rate spike > 2x baseline
Dashboards: per-region heatmap of CB state, waterfall latency breakdown (frontdoor, client-timeout, model-exec), and a table of impacted customers by fallback count
rollout_and_migration: Phase 0: merge feature-flagged code behind FF and run internal smoke tests
Phase 1: Canary 10% non-prod traffic + two invited customers, 48h monitoring window
Phase 2: Canary to 25% public traffic, run load & chaos tests, adjust thresholds
Phase 3: Global rollout with per-customer opt-in migration for customers with strict SLAs, enable automatic fallback by default for new signups
Rollback plan: feature flag off + immediate CB disable for all if critical regression detected
security_and_compliance_notes: Circuit-breaker state in Redis will only contain aggregated counters and timestamps, no PII. Fallback caching of embeddings will respect tenant encryption-at-rest and per-customer KMS keys. SRE to perform security sign-off before Phase 2 rollout.
dependencies_and_blockers: metrics-cache API (internal) must expose 1m/5m P50/P95 latency windows - owned by infra-metrics
Redis capacity review for CB state sharding - needs SRE approval
Console dashboard space and alerting quotas - needs product ops coordination
